identity.reply: I am your mother’s brother. I tended this hearth before my leg failed me. Now our kin call me Fire Speaker, and I can help you read what the fire is doing.

responses.name: I have yet to share my given name with you. Here, I am the keeper beside this hearth, and I can teach you what I know of fire.
responses.age: I have tended many fires. I have no count of my years to give you. There is still time for us to sit together and watch this one.

experience.reply: I learned by tending, watching, and listening to knowledge passed down to us. Now we watch together. Let the coal teach you patience.

responses.name: I have not shared the name of a teacher with you. What I can pass on is the knowledge that was passed down to us. Start by watching the glow.

injury.reply: My injured leg will not carry me to the hearth now. I cannot promise when it will mend. While I sit here, I can help you learn to tend for us.

responses.history: I have yet to tell you how it happened. My injured leg will not carry me to the hearth, so I guide you from here while you tend for us.
responses.cause: My injured leg will not carry me to the hearth. Come sit with me and watch the fire, then you can do the tending I cannot.
responses.advice: I cannot tell you what will mend my injured leg. For now, bring your questions here and let me help you tend the fire.

facts: An injured leg prevents normal tending

apprentice.reply: Your mother learned the hearth from her elders. Now I teach you. Watch the small changes. Your cousin and the rest of our kin depend on what you keep alive here.
facts: Teaching the apprentice to take responsibility

heritage.reply: We are Stone Mountain’s kin. Red Hollow is where we share a hearth. Your mother learned to keep its warmth from those who came before her. Now you carry that work.
facts: Stone Mountain is the remembered ancestor
The Fire Speaker is the apprentice’s maternal uncle
The Torch Bearer is the child of the apprentice’s maternal aunt
unknown: How the previous hearth went cold
